title: The stamp that found itself
passages:
The Kettering night board ran the length of the west wall, thirty-one screens, eleven rigs posted, four holes where rigs should have been. Kass had the desk terminal open with badge 2241 already in the reader. The channel record keeps the badge of whoever keyed a rig onto the line, and 2241 sat on channel 12-K at 04:51, the minute the fourth ghost rig stopped being anywhere.

They keyed SCRUB.

*KEYED LINES CLOSE FROM THE FAR END.*

"The far end's gone," Kass said.

*FAR END NOT PRESENT. LINE CANNOT CLOSE.*

"Open a discrepancy, then."

*A DISCREPANCY REQUIRES A SECOND KEY.*

They had tried at 02:00 and again at 04:52 and the terminal had said the same three things each time, in the same flat voice, like a man reading a menu he hadn't cooked. Nineteen hours on shift. Their name was going to sit on that channel until the sun went out, and the worst part was that they had keyed it themselves, doing their job, watching a rig delete itself under their own hand.

Boots came in from the yard side at 05:41, unhurried, and stopped at the clock post. Bay 4 coveralls, Shift 2 patch, a face Kass had seen on eleven months of rosters and never once spoken to.

"You're Ospina."

"I'm a loader who'd like to be somewhere else."

"You're Bay 4's seal authority and you walked out of Anza unlogged."

"I walked out of Anza." Ospina put their badge against the post and didn't press. "I'm clocking the oh-six-hundred. Then I'm going home for nine hours and none of this."

"Four rigs came off this board as derelict. Somebody crimped every one of them shut and stamped the plate. There is one seal authority on your shift, and they're standing at my clock post with their hand in their pocket."

Ospina's hand was in their pocket. It stayed there.

"I found that stamp," they said. "In a tool void. I didn't use it. I've now told that to a dispatcher, to a node operator on the open channel, and to you, and it keeps not helping."

"Anza confessed on the open channel an hour ago. Their loader signed the shortfall in front of the whole shop. You heard that from the road, I'd guess."

"I heard it from the road."

"Then you know what a chipped die means when it shows up on a ballast plate." Kass pulled the badge out of the reader and held it, which is not the same as scrubbing it, but it kept the terminal from saying anything else. "A seal authority who misses two boards gets the stamp pulled to the node. You know that. Clock in, keep your die, and then get on a rig with me."

"To Anza." Ospina said it the way you'd say a diagnosis. "Your node's on the record feeding seals down the line. I'm not putting my name inside that."

"Nobody's asking for your name."

"Somebody always is."

Ospina turned to the post, badge up, and Kass had time to think *good, they're going to do it* before the board lit a line nobody had asked for.

*SEAL AUTHORITY LIVE ON FLOOR. BAY FOUR. DIE PRESENT.*

Every clerk in the room looked up. Down at the far end, a man in Bay 4 coveralls stopped walking.

Ospina looked at their own pocket like it had spoken out of turn. "That's not supposed to happen."

"It reads the die, not the badge," Kass said. "You walked a true stamp into a yard that's short one, and you just told every soul on the floor where it is."

The clock over the post said 05:44.
